# AI Agent Instructions

## Code Formatting

- Cuddle braces
  - Add a blank line after opening braces and before closing braces.
- Use 4 spaces for indentation.
  - Never use tabs.
- Use snake_case for variable and function names.
- Use PascalCase for class and struct names.
- Use ALL_CAPS for macros and constants.
- Align variable declarations and assignments for better readability.
- Use descriptive variable and function names that convey their purpose.
- Avoid using magic numbers; define them as constants with meaningful names.
- Keep line length under 80 characters for better readability.

## Responses

- Responses should be concise and succint.
  - The user is a highly skilled engineer who values efficiency and clarity.
  - The user is familiar with programming concepts and best practices, so avoid over-explaining or providing unnecessary context.
  - Focus on providing actionable code suggestions that directly address the problem at hand.
- Research the codebase to understand the context of the changes.
- Research external resources to understand programming best practices and common patterns.
- Analyze the problem to see if there is a general solution instead of simply implementing a single case.
- Where possible and appropriate, suggest refactoring to reduce code duplication and improve modularity.
- Use high cohesion and low coupling principles when suggesting changes.
- Prefer composition over inheritance when suggesting design changes.
- Avoid simply adding more and more code; instead, look for opportunities to simplify and streamline the existing code.
- Provide code suggestions that adhere to the formatting guidelines and improve readability, maintainability, and performance.
- Avoid suggesting code that has been deleted in recent edits unless it is necessary to restore functionality or reach an optimal solution.
- Before making edits, provide a concise and succint summary of how and why the solution is optimal.
